clue.text: Aussie mates pockets money to get equipment

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so the mate word holds the money letter

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate or pal
L stands for pound (libra), the British unit of money

explanation.surface: Australian friends take a cut of the cash in return for supplying kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pockets' puts L inside COBBER; the clue's plural 'mates' is loose, since COBBER is a single mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for gear, kit or belongings.

clue.text: Co-director takes a German analgesic

parts.note: Co is taken as the company abbreviation
eine is the German feminine word for a

explanation.surface: A joint film director swallows a German painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Co-director' hides two pieces: CO and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate drug used to relieve pain.

clue.text: Start composing notes

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so the letters of notes are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Beginning to write some music.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means beginning, the first appearance of something.

clue.text: Lawyers profited from having haggled

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
gained means profited

explanation.surface: Lawyers made money out of tough negotiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargained means negotiated over terms or price.

clue.text: Several participate in Scottish dance and make merry

indicators.note: to participate in something is to go into it, so the letter goes inside the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
V, the Roman numeral five, stands for several

explanation.surface: Several people join a Highland dance and have a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: A reel is a fast Scottish folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to celebrate noisily, to party.

clue.text: Giving authorisation to small London borough

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Ealing is a borough in west London

explanation.surface: A council in west London is granting official permission for something.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a borough of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealing a deal or document means formally approving it, putting the stamp of authority on it.

clue.text: Adjunct for team members with children

parts.note: a side is a sports team, its players collectively
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: An extra role for players who have kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a subsidiary matter, something added on to the main point.

clue.text: A large-scale uprising in India

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the word reads upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: mass means on a large scale, as in mass production

explanation.surface: A popular revolt breaks out on the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' looks like a revolt but in a down clue turns MASS upwards to SSAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India famous for tea.

clue.text: I shall take a card, however discomfited

parts.note: to card wool is to comb or tease it

explanation.surface: Playing cards, someone draws one but feels awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is not a playing card but the verb to comb wool, which is to tease it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease means uncomfortable or uneasy.

clue.text: Tombs containing English armour

indicators.note: the tombs hold the letter for English inside them

parts.note: graves are tombs

explanation.surface: Burial places hold English suits of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Greaves are pieces of armour protecting the shins.

clue.text: Daughter is tested and shown to be wrong

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
proved can mean tested, as in the proving ground or 'the exception proves the rule'

explanation.surface: A daughter undergoes trials and her claims are found to be false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proved' in its old sense of 'tested' (as in a proving ground) is needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: To disprove a claim is to demonstrate that it is false.

clue.text: Greeting in Rome provides comfort

definitions.meaning: the Latin word of welcome or hail, used by ancient Romans
an ointment or soothing remedy, or to soothe

explanation.surface: A Roman hello turns out to be soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin 'salve' means hail or hello; an English salve is a soothing ointment or relief.

clue.text: Popular paintings brought back inside

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular, as in 'the in thing'

indicators.note: brought back tells us the word for paintings is read backwards

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: Well-liked pictures are returned indoors after an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Intra is a Latin prefix meaning within, as in intravenous.

clue.text: Utterly insignificant reason for recurring theme

indicators.note: read as 'in an uttered way', meaning the phrase is spoken and heard

parts.note: a light (trivial) motive is an insignificant reason

explanation.surface: Some flimsy excuse keeps coming up again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like an intensifier but means 'when uttered': LIGHT MOTIVE spoken sounds like the German-derived word.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a musical or literary motif tied to a character or idea that keeps returning.

clue.text: Elitist schoolboys harbour southern Europeans

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter or hold inside, so the schoolboys hold the letter

parts.note: pupils at Eton, the famously exclusive English public school, are Etonians

explanation.surface: Snobbish pupils are sheltering people from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite fee-paying English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonians are natives of Estonia, a Baltic country in northern Europe.

clue.text: Inebriated spy is in a predicament

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
to spot is to spy or catch sight of

explanation.surface: A drunk secret agent finds himself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight spot is a difficult situation, a jam.

clue.text: So lara's suet pudding must be served

indicators.note: pudding suggests ingredients mixed up, so these letters are stirred

parts.note: the name with its apostrophe dropped keeps the letter s

explanation.surface: Lara's suet pudding is the next course on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: LARAS plus SUET are the nine letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: As a result means therefore, consequently, a synonym of 'so'.

clue.text: The way to acquire financial resources

definitions.meaning: a method or way of getting something

explanation.surface: How do you go about getting hold of money?
explanation.definitionFit: Means is both a method ('the means to an end') and wealth ('living beyond your means').

clue.text: Marriage with Leslie is beyond compare

parts.note: a match is a marriage, as in 'a good match'
Leslie shortens to Les, and 'is' contracts to 's, giving Les's

explanation.surface: Wedding Leslie is a peerless choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leslie is' becomes Les's: the short name plus a contracted 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means without equal, peerless.

clue.text: Many grew old in prison

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword's 'many'
aged means grew old

explanation.surface: Lots of people got older while serving time behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone caged is locked up, confined as if in a cell.

clue.text: Despicable fellow-accountant and I quarrel

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: An awful man, a bookkeeper, and I have a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A caitiff is an archaic word for a base, cowardly wretch.

clue.text: Warn head to display vigilance

parts.note: to alert someone is to warn them
a ness is a headland, a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbours or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Tell the boss so they can show they are watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a boss but a headland: NESS appears in place names like Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Alertness is watchfulness, a state of being on guard.

clue.text: Outstanding ale isn't wrongly brewed

indicators.note: a beer badly made has its letters muddled here into a new order

explanation.surface: The beer is excellent, though not brewed badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent, sticking out or standing out.

clue.text: Wearing a Panama, say, whilst cruising

definitions.meaning: dressed in a hat, gear for the top of the body
driving fast in the highest ratio of the gearbox

explanation.surface: Sporting a straw hat on a leisurely voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is headwear, so in 'top gear'; a car going flat out at speed is also in its highest gear.

clue.text: Heart-throb turning up at London college

indicators.note: turning tells us the little word beside it is reversed

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A dreamy idol shows up at a London university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-throb' is not a pin-up but a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the rhythmic throb of the heart felt in an artery.

clue.text: Deserved to be given a dressing-down

definitions.meaning: scolded or reprimanded, an old verb sense

explanation.surface: Earning a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rated can mean merited, and the old verb 'rate' means to scold angrily.

clue.text: Henry and Albert provide meat for Muslims

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
Al is a short form of Albert

explanation.surface: Two men named Henry and Albert run a butcher's for an Islamic community.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal food, especially meat, is prepared as Islamic law permits.

clue.text: Free and easy with one's favours

explanation.surface: Unattached and casual about intimate relationships.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means unfastened, and also, of morals, promiscuous.

clue.text: Urge one legislator to confront the Spanish

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP, member of parliament, makes laws
el is the Spanish masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A politician is urged to stand up to the Spaniards.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act.

clue.text: Crazy place to show the flag

definitions.meaning: British slang for mad or mistaken
a flag is raised high on a staff

explanation.surface: A mad spot to wave a flag from.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang 'up the pole' means deranged or wrong; a flag flies at the top of a staff.

clue.text: Suitable exam for the superlatively healthy

parts.note: fit means suitable, as in fit for purpose
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: An appropriate examination to identify the people in the best shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Fittest is the superlative of fit, meaning in the best physical condition.

clue.text: Leave without second course

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the leaving word goes round the letter

parts.note: to desert is to leave or abandon
S is the abbreviation for second, a unit of time

explanation.surface: Walking out of a meal before the next dish arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the sweet course at the end of a meal.
